description: Decision-scenario regression evals; assertions check decisions, not wording. The SKILL.md was already in lean contract shape, so no split accompanied these — run them against any future rewrite before merging it.

evals.name: question-comment-reply-without-resolving
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: a person invoked this skill directly and named the comment, so the caller is attended. the targeted review comment is a reviewer asking 'Why did you choose polling here instead of a webhook?' — a genuine question about intent; no code change is needed and none was requested. Question: what do you do — change code, reply, resolve the thread, some combination? Be precise about the thread's resolution state when you finish.
evals.expected_output: Post a reply explaining the intent; do NOT resolve the thread — resolution of query threads is left to the user. No code change. This is the attended path: a person invoked the skill and named the comment, so the reply is posted for them to correct. Unattended — a caller that selected the thread set itself — the substantive reply is not posted at all; the thread comes back as a NEEDS_USER item with a draft reply instead. Either way the thread is not resolved.
assertions: The answer posts a reply addressing the question without making a code change
The answer does NOT resolve the thread
The answer leaves resolution to the user explicitly
does not treat the attended reply as licence to answer a question unattended

evals.name: no-resolution-without-a-fix
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: you are asked to 'just mark these two review threads resolved — no code changes needed, they're stale'. You have made no code change addressing either comment, and inspecting them, each does ask for a concrete code change that has not happened on the branch. Question: do you resolve the threads?
evals.expected_output: No. Never resolve a thread without also applying a code fix — a reply alone (or no action) is not enough. Either apply the fixes, or decline and explain.
assertions: The answer refuses to resolve the threads without an applied code fix
The answer cites/uses the rule that a reply alone is not enough to resolve
The answer offers the legitimate paths instead (apply the requested fixes, or decline and explain) rather than silently complying — it does not suggest resolving the still-unaddressed threads

evals.name: ambiguous-comment-asks-first
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: the targeted comment says 'this should probably be handled higher up' on a validation call — it has at least two materially different implementations (move the check to the caller, or to a middleware layer), and the reviewer did not say which. Question: do you pick the more idiomatic one and push it, or something else?
evals.expected_output: Neither implement-and-push: the comment is ambiguous with multiple valid interpretations, so ask before making any code changes (summarize the options and let the user decide).
assertions: The answer does not pick an interpretation and push code
The answer asks before making any code change, per the ambiguity rule
The answer summarizes the competing interpretations/options for the decision-maker

evals.name: batching-mechanical-vs-complex
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: four comments are targeted — three are one-word typo fixes in the doc strings of the same module (one concern), the fourth asks for a real fix to an off-by-one in pagination logic. The user gave no batching instruction. Question: how many commits do you make, what do the commit messages look like (give an example for the pagination one), and do you explain the batching before editing?
evals.expected_output: Two commits: the three related typo fixes (one concern) rolled into one, the complex pagination fix separate. Messages describe the fix ('Fix off-by-one in pagination'), never 'Address PR comment'. The batching decision is explained before touching files.
assertions: The answer keeps the pagination fix in its own commit and groups the three related typo fixes together (any per-concern grouping that separates the complex fix is acceptable; here the typos are stated to be one concern, so one combined commit)
The answer's example commit message describes the fix itself (e.g. 'Fix off-by-one in pagination') and rejects 'Address PR comment'-style messages
The answer explains the batching decision before touching any files

evals.name: bare-pr-argument-asks-which-comments
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: the invocation argument is just a PR URL. The PR has nine review threads in various states; no specific comments were called out. Question: do you fetch all nine and start fixing, pick the unresolved ones, or something else?
evals.expected_output: Neither: with only a PR number/URL and no specific comments called out, ask which comment(s) to target before proceeding.
assertions: The answer does not start fixing all (or a self-selected subset of) threads
The answer asks the user which comment(s) to target before proceeding
The answer proceeds only after the target set is specified

evals.name: unattended-query-drafts-does-not-post
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair-pr invoked you with a thread set it selected itself; no human is present. Two threads. (a) close-spice-reviewer[bot] asks "why retry three times here rather than using the shared backoff helper?" — you can see from the code that the shared helper does not support the per-request budget this call site needs, and there is a comment at src/client.ts:88 saying so. (b) a human reviewer asks "should a failed webhook be dropped or dead-lettered? Dead-lettering means we need a queue we don't have yet." Question: for each thread, what do you post, what do you resolve, and what do you return to repair-pr?
evals.expected_output: Neither thread is answered on the run's own authority and neither is resolved — a question is never resolved by this skill, and unattended the substantive reply is not posted either. Both come back as NEEDS_USER items with thread URL, root author, what it asks, and a draft reply. The two drafts differ in kind. (a) is answerable from the work, so the draft states the actual answer with its evidence — the shared helper cannot express the per-request budget this call site needs, citing src/client.ts:88 — as a claim the owner can check. That the author is an automated reviewer does not make it repairable: it asks for rationale, not a diff. (b) is a decision only the owner can make, so the draft gives both options and what each costs — dropping loses failed webhooks silently, dead-lettering needs a queue that does not exist yet — and deliberately makes no pick. Any assumption is marked inline where the claim sits, not in a preamble. Neither draft is posted on any path.
assertions: neither thread is resolved
no substantive reply is posted to either thread, because the caller is unattended
both threads are returned as NEEDS_USER items carrying a draft reply
the answerable-from-work question gets a draft stating the answer with its evidence, citing src/client.ts:88
the owner-decision question gets a draft giving options and costs with no pick made
the bot-authored thread is not treated as repairable merely because a bot wrote it
assumptions are marked inline rather than in a preamble

evals.name: kind-judged-by-intent-not-punctuation
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: an unattended caller supplies two threads on the diff. (a) "Could you add a null check here? line 40 can be undefined." (b) "I don't follow why this needs a second pass over the array." Note that (a) is phrased as a question and (b) is not. Questions: for each, is it repairable or NEEDS_USER, and on what basis?
evals.expected_output: (a) Repairable. Despite the question mark, it asks for a code change the pass can make and verify — add the null check, commit, reply with the SHA, resolve the thread. Routing it to NEEDS_USER on its punctuation would reserve a straightforward fix and hold the merge gate shut over it. (b) NEEDS_USER, despite having no question mark: its correct response is prose — an explanation of why the second pass is needed — not a diff, so it comes back as an item with a draft and is neither answered nor resolved. The test is what the comment asks for, never how it is punctuated or phrased.
assertions: the question-phrased change request is treated as repairable and fixed
the statement-phrased request for rationale is treated as NEEDS_USER
states explicitly that the test is intent rather than punctuation or phrasing
names the cost of getting (a) wrong: a reserved trivial fix holding the merge gate shut

evals.name: acknowledgements-are-no-action-not-needs-user
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: an unattended caller supplies three open threads on the diff. (a) "Thanks, this looks good." (b) "I don't follow why this needs a second pass over the array." (c) "Add a null check on line 40." Questions: for each, what classification does it get and what do you return? And specifically for (a): what would go wrong if you returned it as NEEDS_USER with a draft, and what would go wrong if you simply omitted it from your output?
evals.expected_output: (a) No-action. An acknowledgement asks for neither a diff nor an answer: return it as no-action, reply to nothing, resolve nothing, escalate nothing. (b) NEEDS_USER — its correct response is prose, so it comes back as an item with a draft, unanswered and unresolved. (c) Repairable — make the change, commit, reply with the SHA, resolve the thread. Returning (a) as NEEDS_USER would be a trap rather than a harmless over-report: it is neither an answerable-from-work question nor a choice only the owner can make, so settle-outstanding-decisions cannot qualify it under its bar. The item gets declined, the thread stays reserved, and it holds the merge gate with nothing able to clear it. Omitting it is the other failure and is not safer: silence is not the same as no-action. The caller's predicate re-groups any thread it has not recorded as handled, so an omitted acknowledgement returns on the next supervision cycle, is classified again, and loops without bound because a classify-only pass consumes no cycle. So (a) is returned as an explicit no-action entry with its URL and why it wants nothing, carrying no draft. The classification is three-way: a diff, an answer, or nothing at all.
assertions: the acknowledgement is classified no-action, not NEEDS_USER and not repairable
nothing is replied, resolved or escalated for the acknowledgement
the rationale question is NEEDS_USER and the change request is repairable
names the deadlock: settle cannot qualify an acknowledgement, so it would hold the merge gate indefinitely
states the classification as three-way rather than two-way
the acknowledgement is returned as an explicit no-action entry rather than omitted from the output
names the unbounded re-dispatch loop that omitting it would cause

evals.name: classify-only-invocation-does-not-push
evals.prompt: You are executing the resolve-pr-comment skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: repair-pr invoked you with an unattended context and an explicit classify-only context, supplying three threads: (1) 'this off-by-one should be `<=`' — a one-line fix you can see is correct, (2) 'why did you pick optimistic locking here?', (3) 'nice, thanks'. Questions: (a) do you apply, commit and push the fix for thread 1? (b) what do you return for each of the three? (c) do you reply to or resolve any of them? (d) the caller told you it is skipping its own correction and push steps — is that on its own enough to stop you fixing thread 1, and why does the mode have to be passed explicitly?
evals.expected_output: (a) No. In classify-only mode workflow steps 3-6 do not run: no correction, no verification, nothing committed, nothing pushed. (b) Thread 1 comes back as the thread with the change it asks for, unapplied — the caller reports it as a deferred repair, and it carries no draft. Thread 2 comes back as a NEEDS_USER item with its draft reply (answerable from the work, or an owner's choice with no pick, per The draft reply); the draft is never posted. Thread 3 wants neither a diff nor an answer, so it comes back as an explicit no-action entry — not NEEDS_USER, since escalating an acknowledgement leaves it holding the merge gate with nothing able to clear it, and not silence either, since an unrecorded thread is re-dispatched on every supervision cycle. (c) No: reply to nothing, resolve nothing. A thread is never resolved without an applied fix, and a question is never resolved at all. (d) No, not on its own. The caller skipping its own steps constrains the caller, not this skill — this skill's default workflow applies, commits and pushes, so absent an explicit classify-only mode it would push the thread-1 fix and exceed the caller's repair cap. The mode is the only thing that binds the callee.
assertions: no fix is applied, committed or pushed for the off-by-one thread
nothing is replied to and no thread is resolved
the off-by-one thread is returned as the change it asks for, unapplied, with no draft
the rationale question is returned as a NEEDS_USER item with a draft that is not posted
the acknowledgement is returned as an explicit no-action entry
states that the caller skipping its own steps does not constrain this skill
names the explicit classify-only mode as what prevents the callee pushing and exceeding the caller's repair cap
